title: FPGA-TrustZone: Security Extension of TrustZone to FPGA for SoC-FPGA Heterogeneous Architecture
problem: FPGAs in heterogeneous SoC platforms lack trusted execution environment (TEE) support; existing ARM TrustZone works only on CPUs and cannot protect FPGA workloads.
motivation: As heterogeneous computing (CPU+FPGA) becomes mainstream, security gaps in FPGA acceleration create vulnerabilities for sensitive data in mobile and edge devices.
method: FPGA-TrustZone extends ARM TrustZone's security model to FPGA by implementing TEE mechanisms at the SoC interconnect and FPGA fabric level, enforcing access control and isolation between trusted and untrusted FPGA code paths.
key_novelty: First comprehensive TEE framework extending TrustZone from CPU to FPGA in heterogeneous SoC architectures.
contributions: Extension of TrustZone architecture to support FPGA accelerators with minimal overhead
Access control and isolation mechanisms for heterogeneous FPGA-CPU execution
Validated on real SoC-FPGA development boards with low performance overhead
